html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Integrated Year-End NFP Analysis

Apply multiple not-for-profit accounting concepts to determine contribution recognition and ending net assets.

Scenario

Helping Hands Foundation begins the year with:

Net Assets Without Donor Restrictions $400,000
Net Assets With Donor Restrictions $150,000

During the year, the Foundation has the following transactions:

  • Receives an unconditional contribution of $100,000 with no donor restrictions.
  • Receives an unconditional contribution of $120,000 restricted by the donor for educational programs.
  • Receives $60,000 cash under a conditional agreement. The required barrier has not yet been substantially overcome.
  • Uses $70,000 of previously donor-restricted resources for qualifying educational expenses.
  • Receives qualifying donated legal services with a fair value of $20,000. The NFP would otherwise have purchased the services.
  • Other operating expenses during the year total $90,000.

Required

1. Contribution Revenue Without Donor Restrictions From Cash Contribution
2. Contribution Revenue With Donor Restrictions
3. Liability From Conditional Contribution
4. Ending Net Assets With Donor Restrictions
5. Ending Net Assets Without Donor Restrictions
explanation:
Item 1 — Unrestricted Contribution

Contribution Revenue Without Donor Restrictions = $100,000

Item 2 — Restricted Contribution

Contribution Revenue With Donor Restrictions = $120,000

Item 3 — Conditional Contribution

The $60,000 was received before the required contribution barrier was substantially overcome.

Contribution Revenue = $0 Liability = $60,000

Item 4 — Ending Net Assets With Donor Restrictions

Beginning $150,000 + Restricted Contribution $120,000 − Release From Restriction $70,000 = $200,000

Item 5 — Ending Net Assets Without Donor Restrictions

Start with beginning net assets without donor restrictions and include:

  • + $100,000 unrestricted contribution
  • + $70,000 release from restriction
  • + $20,000 qualifying donated legal-service contribution revenue
  • − $20,000 legal expense
  • − $90,000 other operating expenses
Beginning $400,000 + $100,000 + $70,000 + $20,000 − $20,000 − $90,000 = $480,000
